assumptions: The two populations are gated in the same run (the same file, compensation and gating).
limits: Overton cumulative subtraction is not offered: no runnable implementation is known.
With thousands of events every test reports tiny p-values for differences too small to matter.
bio.jane/contract.question: Does this channel differ between these two populations, and by which test?

description: One channel of an FCS file between two populations of the run (FlowJo's and FCS Express's population comparison): Welch's two-sample t-test, the Wilcoxon rank-sum test, the two-sample Kolmogorov–Smirnov test and Pearson's χ² on the two histograms over shared equal-width bins, each R's test on the populations' linear values.

_files.description: The project: record references shaped like _subject. Their records become library documents a tool names in sequences/parts/document; a trace or alignment is found by file name.

_subject.description: The record to act on: exactly one of sequence, accession (+source), sample (an id from list_samples) or file ({name, text} or {name, base64}); record_index picks one record of several.

asinh_a.description: the a in asinh(a + b·x) + c.

asinh_b.description: the b in asinh(a + b·x) + c.

asinh_c.description: the c in asinh(a + b·x) + c.

compare_bins.description: equal-width histogram bins over both populations’ range, for the χ² test.

compare_channel.description: the channel compared (PnN, PnS or a derived name); empty for the first fluorescence channel.

document.description: the FCS file in the project, by name or id.

gating.description: a Gating-ML or FlowJo .wsp in the project; empty for none.

pb_levels.description: probability-binning levels (2^levels bins cut from population A); 0 for flowFP's own rule, floor(log2 n(A)) − 3.

population_a.description: population A; empty for all events.

population_b.description: population B; empty for all events.

name: compare_flow_cytometry_populations

pb_t.description: probability-binning T(χ) of B against A, unitless; above 4 the distributions differ at p < 0.01

tests.description: every test: method, statistic, parameter, p-value; the χ² histograms; the probability-binning counts
